      Problem: The entire `PRIOR_COMMENTS` variable is passed as a single argument to `printf`. If `PRIOR_COMMENTS` is very large (e.g., many prior issue comments), this can exceed the system ARG_MAX, causing `printf` to fail with "Argument list too long". With `set -o pipefail`, the pipeline exits non‑zero and the fingerprint check is silently skipped.; Cross‑cycle escalation fails to detect repeated failures, potentially leading to infinite fix‑up loops and exhausting validation cycles before a human is alerted. This undermines the PR's safety net.

  [4] File: scripts/validate_process.sh (line ~2232)
      Problem: FAILURE_FINGERPRINT="$(jq -r '.fix_issues | sort_by(.title // "") | map(.title // "") | join("\n")' "${DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE}" 2>/dev/null \; | sha256sum \; | cut -c1-16)"; If `jq` fails (e.g., malformed JSON, missing fields), the pipeline produces empty output, which `sha256sum` hashes to the empty string fingerprint "e3b0c...". This yields a non‑empty but meaningless fingerprint. The condition `[ -n "${FAILURE_FINGERPRINT}" ]` will succeed, but the fingerprint will never match any real one, causing escalation to never trigger.; When the diagnose output is invalid, the escalation mechanism is bypassed without a clear signal, allowing repeated failing cycles to continue indefinitely.; Suggested fix: Check the exit status of `jq` and set `FAILURE_FINGERPRINT=""` on failure. For example:; if jq -e '.fix_issues' "${DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then; FAILURE_FINGERPRINT="$(jq -r '.fix_issues | sort_by(.title // "") | map(.title // "") | join("\n")' "${DIAGNOSE_RESULT_FILE}" | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"; FAILURE_FINGERPRINT=""
